title: I’m building an AI pipeline framework to help people build games and learn Godot.
author: AdLegal947
selftext:
I’m building a game-development tool that combines Claude Code with custom UI to help people create games.

I started this project because I want to create my dream game, but I do not have enough time to go through the entire traditional development process. I enjoy coding, artistic decisions, and creative direction much more than spending most of my time working inside a game engine.

This tool is my attempt to make that process faster and more enjoyable, so I can focus on the parts of game development that excite me most.

The project is still a proof of concept, but I already shipped version **0.1.6 during the first week**.

I’m excited about the progress so far and curious to see how far I can take it.

Github: Framework  
First Prototype: [https://arthur0n.itch.io/xfpixel-fps-demo-1](https://arthur0n.itch.io/xfpixel-fps-demo-1)

comments.author: SaltAddictedMan
comments.body: sounds interesting, but link is broken on my end

comments.author: Binoui
comments.body: What does your tool bring that agentic coding doesn't? If your target user is a developper, explain what do they gain from using your tool

replies.author: AdLegal947
replies.body:
I think it brings together self contained agents using different models, specialized prompts, and evaluations, while giving people more freedom to do what they enjoy most.

I’m not aware of any tool trying to do the same thing: being self contained, self improving, and adapting to both the project and the user.

My target audience is anyone who knows a bit about coding, not only developers, and, most importantly, wants to create games.

But hey, if a year from now no one cares and I still ship my game, I’ll be super happy 😄

replies.author: Binoui
replies.body:
Don't worry I'm in the same boat as you, trying to code a game and getting pushback because of ai use. Current mentality will evolve.

From the sounds of it you created your own harness which is cool. Not sure it's better than using any existing one like codex, claude code, anti gravity, openclaw, ... I personally like Hermes agent which is pretty good as self learning because of evolves its own skills

replies.author: AdLegal947
replies.body:
Please don’t understanding me wrong, and please don’t think this is an AI generated answer 😃 because I’m saying that you’re right to push back.

I really like these conversations, and your question made me think and update my README because this is genuine pushback.

I may be biased because I’m building this and have spent years(now) building agents for other people and companies, but my way of thinking is not about working against them or need to choose one. It’s about working together.

I had plans to include Hermes in my loop, and now you’ve made me commit to it 😄

But seriously, in my experience, we’re not there yet when it comes to letting agents work completely on their own. I want to build something specifically for games, on top of the Godot(Redoto and Blazium) ecosystem, while still being able to plug in any new shiny tool, like Hermes or Claw.
